title: Samsung Slams iPhone Duo “Crackgate” in Bold Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ad Campaign【Video】
body:
Samsung has taken a bold swipe at Apple’s latest iPhone misstep, turning the “crackgate” controversy surrounding the iPhone 15 Duo into a centerpiece of its new Galaxy Z Fold 8 advertising campaign. The Korean giant’s commercials juxtapose the fragile glass of the iPhone with the durability claims of its own foldable flagship, urging consumers to consider the Fold 8 as a more reliable alternative. The move marks one of the most direct attacks in the ongoing rivalry between the two tech titans, and it arrives just weeks after Apple’s newest handset suffered a wave of reports describing screens that shattered or cracked under everyday use.

The ads, which debuted on Samsung’s official YouTube channel and across social media platforms, feature a split‑screen visual: on the left, a cracked iPhone 15 Duo screen shatters under a light tap; on the right, the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s hinge mechanism flexes smoothly, followed by a tagline that reads, “Built to bend, built to last.” A voice‑over underscores the message, suggesting that Samsung’s engineering “doesn’t crack under pressure.” By framing the iPhone’s issue as a systemic flaw, Samsung aims to position its foldable as the premium choice for users who value durability as much as innovation.

Apple’s iPhone 15 Duo, released earlier this month, introduced a dual‑screen design that stacks two displays vertically, a departure from the company’s traditional single‑screen format. While the concept generated buzz, early adopters quickly reported that the lower screen—made of the same glass used on the flagship model—was prone to cracking when placed on uneven surfaces or subjected to minor impacts. Consumer watchdog groups have logged thousands of complaints, prompting Apple to issue a statement acknowledging “isolated incidents” and promising a “thorough investigation.” However, the company has not yet announced a formal recall or a repair program, leaving many customers uneasy.

Samsung’s timing is strategic. The Galaxy Z Fold 8, slated for launch later this quarter, represents the latest iteration of the company’s foldable line, featuring a reinforced “Armor Aluminum” frame, a new ultra‑thin glass for the cover display, and an upgraded hinge that Samsung claims can survive over 200,000 folds. By highlighting these durability metrics, Samsung not only defends its own product line but also leverages Apple’s current PR challenge to attract consumers who might be reconsidering a premium smartphone purchase. Industry analysts note that such comparative advertising is rare in the high‑end segment, where brands typically avoid direct attacks to maintain a veneer of mutual respect.

The campaign also taps into a broader narrative about the trade‑off between cutting‑edge design and practical resilience. Foldable phones have long been marketed as the future of mobile computing, yet they have struggled to overcome skepticism about their long‑term reliability. Samsung’s emphasis on “built to last” attempts to reassure wary buyers that the Fold 8 is not merely a novelty but a mature, everyday device. If successful, the ads could shift consumer perception and accelerate the mainstream adoption of foldables—a market that, despite steady growth, still represents a fraction of global smartphone sales.

Critics, however, warn that Samsung’s approach could backfire if Apple swiftly addresses the crack issue with a comprehensive repair program or a hardware revision. Apple’s brand loyalty remains robust, and many users may view Samsung’s mockery as opportunistic rather than informative. Moreover, the ad’s focus on durability does not address other factors that influence purchasing decisions, such as ecosystem integration, software updates, and price points. As both companies prepare for the holiday shopping season, the battle for consumer dollars will likely hinge on how each resolves its respective product challenges.

Looking ahead, the “crackgate” saga may serve as a catalyst for broader industry scrutiny of smartphone durability standards. Regulators and consumer advocacy groups could push for more stringent testing and clearer warranty policies, compelling manufacturers to prioritize robust materials alongside innovative form factors. For Samsung, the success of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 campaign will be measured not just in sales figures but in its ability to reshape the narrative around foldable technology—transforming a perceived weakness into a selling point. Apple, meanwhile, faces the task of restoring confidence in its newest design, a challenge that could influence the company’s product roadmap for years to come.
